analysis: The closest response retains substantial psychological foundations, development, mental health and cognition, now with direct organisational psychology and empirical data/statistical-learning content replacing general social theory, free-will philosophy and physiology. These are bounded repairs to strengthen the target’s actual work/social, behavioural-data and cognitive methods. Clinical/health replaces civil-society theory with data methods while retaining physiology, epidemiology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and ethics. Social/organisational replaces a second rhetorical-education project and free-will philosophy with behavioural economics and data methods. Concepts precede their implementation.

The clinical and social/workplace concepts remain distinct programme-interest clusters, with coherent completed course contributions. Every pair exceeds thirty EC each way. Methods and Clinical Neuropsychology remain evidenced but unattempted after the cap, without any no-match claim. The bilingual registry target permits the Dutch-only neuropsychology direction; the selected Brain/Cognition pathway remains unchanged.

Every selected contribution was read against profile evidence or description-only evidence. Behavioural Economics, Perception/Action and Psycholinguistics receive consideration within what their descriptions support. Pharmacology explicitly includes nervous-system drugs and psychoactive-drug inquiry, correcting the earlier false denial. Leadership-under-pressure includes an actual psychological survey, replacing the stale diversity-management name and supporting its empirical-research correspondence. Linguistic stylistics is a specific complement to social interpretation, not workplace-psychology training.

Recomputed all twenty comparator placements from actual contents after the course changes and expansion of the thirty-credit specialisation. Thirteen relationships concern substantive subjects or methods and expressly limit scope. Clinical interviewing/assessment is a stronger placement for Psychological Communication than generic rhetoric. The original survey/psychological measurement course is the strongest available relationship to Psychological Research; qualitative inquiry contributes elsewhere. Removed the arbitrary Youth Resilience/Current Topics and Persuasion/Current Topics pairs. Statistical learning is the strongest relationship to Behavioural Data Science; generic data cleaning is left unpaired rather than treated as equivalent to its predictive/psychological subject matter. Dedicated neural measurement/Python, simulation/PsychoPy, consciousness topic, first-year thesis, bachelor thesis AI/psychology, and open space retain seven justified gaps.

Two original offering conflicts are repaired by placing Psycholinguistics in its only planned term after Brain/Behavior, concurrently with Neurobiology. No formal Neurobiology prerequisite is invented. Introductory psychology and methods precede advanced statistical study, Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions, statistics precedes meta-analysis, and data foundations precede machine learning. All three schedules have twenty-four unique courses, four each term, first-year PPD and at least six advanced courses. All actual formal prerequisites and assigned offerings are directly verified. Optional independent research is aligned with the actual bachelor thesis outside scheduled credits.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, civic collaboration and reflective practice provide the first-year common foundation.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.contribution: uses psychology-informed biases, heuristics, framing and experiments to examine departures from traditional economic decision models; this directly supports the social-decision strand within the scope of its description

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: develops measurement, empirical design, sampling, statistics and a student data-collection project as foundations for psychological research

BENLEAD111.name: Personal Leadership
BENLEAD111.contribution: examines self-leadership, personality and emotional intelligence in group dynamics, with reflective leadership cases and a personal development plan rather than clinical diagnosis

BENLEAD112.name: Leadership Communication
BENLEAD112.contribution: examines leadership communication, persuasion, emotional intelligence, culture and ethics through leader interviews, advisory analysis and rhetorical practice

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.contribution: examines emotion regulation, belonging, identity and psychological safety in leadership, with an original quantitative psychological survey, measurement, data analysis and empirical reporting

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: directly examines personality, perception, emotions, motivation, group dynamics, leadership, culture and organisational change, with research plans and a systematic literature review

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
BENLEAD312.contribution: examines bargaining, framing, power, emotions, trust and culture through negotiation theory and repeated simulations, implementing social decision-making in practice

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: develops data cleaning, transformation, visualisation and an applied research workflow in R, materially supporting empirical behavioural inquiry

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: develops regression, classification, prediction, model evaluation and statistical learning on real data, supporting the cognitive and behavioural-data focus without claiming a psychology-specific AI course

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: develops ethical theories and reasoned analysis of moral problems as a complementary basis for evaluating choices in assessment, treatment and health

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.contribution: examines mind, consciousness, identity, physicalism and neuropsychological cases through philosophical argument, complementing empirical cognition

GOSPHIL311.name: Philosophy of Emotion
GOSPHIL311.contribution: examines theories of emotion and their relationship to knowledge, decisions, ethics and social life through philosophical analysis, complementing empirical psychological accounts

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: examines socialisation, interaction, inequality and institutions as social mechanisms shaping individual and group behaviour, complementing the psychological explanations

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops qualitative research design, interviews, observation, coding and interpretation for studying human experience and social behaviour

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.contribution: examines modern sociological explanations of social order, inequality, identity and institutions as a structural complement to social and organisational psychology

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: examines civil society, solidarity, trust and exclusion as mechanisms of collective life, supporting the social-group focus alongside individual psychological explanation

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: develops epidemiological designs, bias, confounding and causal interpretation for evaluating disease patterns and health evidence; mental-health applications are not a separate taught specialism

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: examines drug action, kinetics, metabolism, toxicity and pharmacogenomics, including nervous-system drugs and a psychoactive-drug research proposal, supporting the health and mental-disorder strand

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.contribution: connects organ regulation and dysfunction to endocrine, nervous-system and other disease mechanisms through clinical cases, providing a biomedical complement to psychological disorder

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: examines comparative neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, animal behaviour, sleep and rhythms, with biological explanations of behaviour and laboratory introductions

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: examines neural mechanisms of sensory information processing and goal-directed action through cognitive-neuroscience and neuropsychological approaches

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: examines attention, memory, emotion, cognitive control and consciousness through neural function and dysfunction, an attentional-blink experiment and a research proposal

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines neural and psychological mechanisms of language acquisition, comprehension and production, language impairments and experimental approaches within the scope of its description

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: introduces cells, biomolecules, metabolism, heredity and gene expression as biological foundations for the neural and health dimensions of psychology

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces neural signalling, brain organisation, development, learning and behavioural/neuroscience research as direct foundations for brain-behaviour study

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: examines homeostasis, neuroendocrine signalling and integrated organ-system regulation, giving the clinical/health option a biological account of brain-body interaction

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: directly examines social cognition, attitudes, influence, groups and interpersonal behaviour through empirical studies and a research proposal

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: develops experimental design, multivariable statistical models and data-analysis reporting in health and behavioural research

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: directly examines mental disorders through biological, psychological, social and cultural explanations, case analysis and a structured literature study

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: examines stress, symptoms, illness and health behaviour through biological, psychological and social interactions

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: directly examines psychological tests, interviews, assessment and major therapy approaches, with introductory skills training and a psychodiagnostic case report; it confers no professional qualification

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: develops systematic review and quantitative meta-analysis, effect sizes, heterogeneity, bias and research reporting in behavioural and medical inquiry

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: directly examines physical, cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan, with biological/environmental influences and a life-story study

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
HCBPSYC315.contribution: examines youth radicalisation, developmental risk and protective factors, belonging and social-emotional learning, applying research in educational prevention materials

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: develops rhetorical analysis, argument and persuasive speaking as applied social communication, without substituting for psychologist interviewing training

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.contribution: examines how grammar, discourse, schemas, modality and construal shape interpretation, principally in literary texts, as a linguistic complement to social communication rather than workplace-psychology training

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: examines coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation and cognitive shortcuts through communication research and community projects on behaviour change

alignment.rationale: Both develop empirical design, measurement, statistical testing and data analysis. UCR applies these across disciplines; UvA establishes the psychology-specific sequence.

Both involve psychological measurement, original data collection, quantitative analysis and empirical reporting. UCR studies leadership-related survey questions; UvA additionally constructs a psychological test and provides its prescribed test-theory sequence.

Both substantively examine statistical prediction and machine-learning approaches to data. UCR develops regression, classification and model evaluation in depth; UvA introduces behavioural big data, latent variables, network analysis and prediction from a psychology perspective.

Both examine the nature of mind, physical explanation and conceptual problems behind psychological science. UCR emphasises philosophy of mind; UvA also examines the history and general foundations of psychology.
Both examine neural anatomy, physiology and mechanisms underlying behaviour. UvA builds explicitly from molecular/cellular mechanisms to cortical and subcortical networks and research techniques.
Both examine sensory processing and the neural relationship between perception and action. UvA also addresses attention, multisensory integration and consciousness.

Both examine memory and emotion through cognitive neuroscience and neural dysfunction. UvA also gives substantial explicit coverage to language, while UCR includes attention, control and consciousness.
Both introduce brain organisation, mental processes and the relationship between neural function and behaviour. UvA also surveys the whole discipline of psychology.
Both substantively examine social cognition, attitudes, influence and group processes. The combined UvA component additionally covers work and organisational psychology.
Both develop empirical research design, statistical models and critical interpretation of psychological findings. UvA explicitly integrates scientific argumentation.
Both examine psychological disorder, symptoms, explanatory models and clinical perspectives. UvA additionally provides a distinct neurological-disorder and neuropsychology introduction.

Both develop psychological interviewing, reflection and interpersonal assessment skills. UCR embeds introductory practice in clinical assessment and therapy; UvA provides a dedicated general psychological-communication practical.
Both examine physical, cognitive, emotional and social development and biological/environmental influences across the lifespan.
No selected UCR course is a separately credited first-year psychology thesis.

Selected courses contribute experimental design, cognitive experiments and data methods elsewhere, but none reproduces this dedicated combination of neuroscientific measurement, behavioural paradigms and Python experiment/programming practice.

Advanced statistics, meta-analysis and computational study are represented elsewhere. None is counted again as this dedicated course in simulation studies, mathematical cognitive-task models and Python/PsychoPy experiment construction.
The 12-EC Brain and Cognition empirical thesis is compulsory at UvA. Optional UCR independent research is shown separately outside scheduled credits.
Higher cognitive study has its strongest placement with Memory, Language and Emotion. No additional course is counted as this dedicated experimental, neuroscientific and clinical consciousness topic.

The strongest selected statistical-learning relationship is placed with Behavioural Data Science. No additional course is counted as this integrated account of AI and psychology, their shared history and contemporary applications and ethics.
The thirty-credit optional profile is genuinely open; no particular minor, exchange host or course package is invented.
